## 1. Purpose

This procedure describes the selection, design, and validation of
primers and probes targeting functional genes of the nitrogen cycle for
use with droplet digital PCR (ddPCR). The nitrogen cycle genes covered
include those encoding nitrification (*amoA* for both ammonia-oxidizing
bacteria and archaea), denitrification (*nirK*, *nirS*, *nosZ*),
nitrogen fixation (*nifH*), and dissimilatory nitrate reduction to
ammonium (*nrfA*). The SOP covers literature-based primer selection,
in silico evaluation, and bench validation on the Bio-Rad QX200 ddPCR
system [@hindson2011; @biorad_qx200_2024].


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** Design and selection of primers and hydrolysis probes
  (TaqMan) or EvaGreen-based assays for quantifying nitrogen cycle
  functional genes from environmental DNA extracts (soil, sediment,
  water)
- **Does not apply to:** Amplicon sequencing library preparation,
  metagenomics, or RNA-based transcript quantification (RT-ddPCR)
- **Location:** Molecular biology bench, Pomona College Biogeochemistry
  Lab


## 3. Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve primer selections and assay designs |
| Trained Personnel | Conduct in silico analysis, order primers, perform validation runs |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use    |


## 4. Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** ddPCR droplet generation oil contains proprietary
  surfactants; avoid skin and eye contact. EvaGreen and other
  intercalating dyes are potential mutagens at high concentrations;
  handle with gloves.
- **Physical:** The QX200 Droplet Generator uses pressurized cartridges.
  Follow manufacturer instructions for cartridge handling.
- **Biological:** Environmental DNA extracts may originate from samples
  containing pathogens. Handle with standard precautions.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves (changed frequently)

### Emergency Procedures

For chemical splash, flush with water for 15 minutes. Refer to
[SOP-L02 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L02-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd).

## 6. Procedure

### 6.1 Target Gene Selection

The nitrogen cycle encompasses multiple functional transformations. The
table below lists the primary target genes, the enzymatic step they
represent, and key references for established primer sets
[@braker2000; @rotthauwe1997; @rosch2002; @henry2006; @poly2001;
@welsh2014]:

| Gene    | Enzyme                        | Process                                | Organism Group      |
|:--------|:------------------------------|:---------------------------------------|:--------------------|
| *amoA*  | Ammonia monooxygenase         | Ammonia oxidation (nitrification)      | AOB, AOA            |
| *nirK*  | Copper-containing nitrite reductase | Denitrification (NO~2~^-^ to NO) | Denitrifiers        |
| *nirS*  | Cytochrome cd~1~ nitrite reductase | Denitrification (NO~2~^-^ to NO)  | Denitrifiers        |
| *nosZ*  | Nitrous oxide reductase       | Denitrification (N~2~O to N~2~)        | Denitrifiers (Clade I and II) |
| *nifH*  | Nitrogenase reductase         | Nitrogen fixation (N~2~ to NH~3~)      | Diazotrophs         |
| *nrfA*  | Cytochrome c nitrite reductase| DNRA (NO~2~^-^ to NH~4~^+^)           | DNRA organisms      |

### 6.2 Literature-Based Primer Selection

1. Search the published literature for validated primer sets targeting
   each gene of interest. Prioritized references include
   @rotthauwe1997, @francis2005, @braker2000, @henry2006, @poly2001,
   @jones2013, and @welsh2014.
2. For each candidate primer pair, record: primer names, sequences
   (5' to 3'), amplicon length, annealing temperature, and the original
   publication.
3. Evaluate published primer sets against the following criteria:

   a. Amplicon length between 60 and 200 bp (optimal for ddPCR; shorter
      amplicons partition more efficiently into droplets) [@hindson2011]
   b. Demonstrated use in environmental samples similar to your matrix
      (e.g., soil, sediment)
   c. Broad coverage of the target gene clade verified by in silico
      analysis (see 6.3)
   d. Minimal off-target amplification in non-target organisms

::: {.callout-note}
Many classic nitrogen cycle primers (e.g., *nosZ* primers nosZ-F/nosZ-R
from @henry2006) were designed for conventional qPCR with amplicons of
250--400 bp. These may need to be redesigned or replaced with shorter
alternatives optimized for ddPCR. Consult @biorad_qx200_2024 for
amplicon length recommendations.
:::

### 6.3 In Silico Primer Evaluation

1. Check primer specificity using NCBI Primer-BLAST
   (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/tools/primer-blast/) against the nr/nt
   database, restricting the search to bacteria and/or archaea as
   appropriate [@ye2012]
2. Verify primer coverage against curated functional gene databases:
   a. FunGene (http://fungene.cme.msu.edu/) for *amoA*, *nirK*, *nirS*,
      *nosZ*, *nifH* [@fish2013]
   b. *TBD -- identify additional databases for nrfA coverage analysis*
3. Check for primer dimers and secondary structures using IDT OligoAnalyzer
   (https://www.idtdna.com/calc/analyzer) or Primer3
   (https://primer3.ut.ee/)
4. Confirm that the melting temperature (T~m~) of each primer falls
   between 55 and 65 C, with no more than 2 C difference between
   forward and reverse primers
5. For hydrolysis probe (TaqMan) assays, design the probe to have a
   T~m~ 5--10 C higher than the primers, with no G at the 5' end
   (quenches FAM fluorescence), and a length of 15--30 bases
   [@biorad_qx200_2024]

### 6.4 Recommended Primer Sets

The following table summarizes commonly used primer sets for nitrogen
cycle genes. Confirm suitability for your specific sample type and ddPCR
platform before use.

::: {.callout-important}
This table provides a starting point. Primer sequences, annealing
temperatures, and amplicon sizes should be verified against current
literature and databases before ordering. Some primer sets listed below
produce amplicons longer than ideal for ddPCR and may require
redesign.
:::

| Gene    | Primer Name     | Sequence (5' to 3')            | Amplicon (bp) | Reference             | ddPCR Suitability |
|:--------|:----------------|:-------------------------------|:--------------|:----------------------|:------------------|
| *amoA* (AOB) | amoA-1F / amoA-2R | GGGGTTTCTACTGGTGGT / CCCCTCKGSAAAGCCTTCTTC | 491 | @rotthauwe1997 | Redesign needed (too long) |
| *amoA* (AOA) | Arch-amoAF / Arch-amoAR | STAATGGTCTGGCTTAGACG / GCGGCCATCCATCTGTATGT | 635 | @francis2005 | Redesign needed (too long) |
| *nirK*  | nirK876 / nirK1040 | ATYGGCGGVCAYGGCGA / GCCTCGATCAGRTTRTGGTT | 165 | @henry2006 | Suitable |
| *nirS*  | cd3aF / R3cd   | GTSAACGTSAAGGARACSGG / GASTTCGGRTGSGTCTTGA | 410 | @braker2000 | Redesign needed |
| *nosZ* (Clade I) | nosZ2F / nosZ2R | CGCRACGGCAASAAGGTSMSSGT / CAKRTGCAKSGCRTGGCAGAA | 267 | @henry2006 | Marginal; consider shorter alternative |
| *nosZ* (Clade II) | nosZ-II-F / nosZ-II-R | CTIGGICCIYTKCAYAC / GCIGARCARAAITCBGTRC | 698 | @jones2013 | Redesign needed |
| *nifH*  | PolF / PolR     | TGCGAYCCSAARGCBGACTC / ATSGCCATCATYTCRCCGGA | 360 | @poly2001 | Redesign needed |
| *nrfA*  | nrfAF2aw / nrfAR1 | CARTGYCAYGTBGARTA / TWNGGCATRTGRCARTC | 251 | @welsh2014 | Marginal |

*TBD -- update this table with ddPCR-optimized primer sets as they are
validated in the lab. Short-amplicon redesigns for amoA, nirS, nosZ
Clade II, and nifH are in progress.*

### 6.5 Primer and Probe Ordering

1. Order desalted primers at 25 nmol scale from IDT (Integrated DNA
   Technologies) or equivalent supplier
2. Order hydrolysis probes HPLC-purified with 5'-FAM (or HEX for
   multiplexing) and 3'-Iowa Black FQ quencher
3. For positive controls, order synthetic double-stranded DNA fragments
   (gBlocks) matching the target amplicon sequence. Include at least
   50 bp of flanking sequence on each side of the primer binding sites.
4. Resuspend lyophilized primers in nuclease-free water to a stock
   concentration of 100 uM. Store at --20 C.
5. Prepare 10 uM working stocks by diluting 1:10 in nuclease-free water.
   Store at --20 C.

### 6.6 ddPCR Thermal Cycling Optimization

1. Set up a temperature gradient experiment on the Bio-Rad C1000 Touch
   to determine the optimal annealing temperature for each primer set
2. Use a thermal gradient spanning the predicted T~m~ minus 5 C to T~m~
   plus 5 C (typically 55--65 C)
3. Use positive control gBlock DNA diluted to approximately 1,000 copies
   per uL as template
4. Recommended cycling protocol (adjust annealing temperature per
   gradient results) [@biorad_qx200_2024]:

   a. Enzyme activation: 95 C for 10 min
   b. 40 cycles of:
      - Denaturation: 94 C for 30 s
      - Annealing/extension: *gradient temperature* for 60 s
   c. Signal stabilization: 98 C for 10 min
   d. Hold at 4 C (indefinite)
   e. Ramp rate: 2 C/s for all steps

5. Read droplets on the QX200 Droplet Reader
6. Select the annealing temperature that produces the clearest separation
   between positive and negative droplet clusters in the QuantaSoft
   amplitude plot

::: {.callout-tip}
### Tip
If positive and negative droplet populations overlap ("rain"), try
increasing the annealing temperature by 1--2 C or reducing the primer
concentration from 900 nM to 450 nM. Excessive rain suggests non-specific
amplification or suboptimal primer binding [@lievens2016].
:::

### 6.7 Assay Validation

1. **Specificity:** Run no-template controls (NTC) and extraction blanks
   from [SOP-L80](SOP-L80-dna-extraction.qmd) to confirm the absence of
   false positives
2. **Dynamic range:** Prepare a serial dilution of gBlock positive
   control (10 to 100,000 copies per reaction) and verify linearity of
   the ddPCR response across the range [@huggett2013]
3. **Limit of detection (LOD):** Determine the lowest copy number that
   produces a statistically significant positive call above the NTC
   background. For ddPCR, this is typically 1--10 copies per 20 uL
   reaction [@hindson2011]
4. **Matrix effects:** Run environmental DNA extracts at multiple
   dilutions (undiluted, 1:5, 1:10) to check for PCR inhibition. If
   inhibition is detected, the 1:10 dilution value (back-calculated)
   should agree within 20% of the 1:5 value [@racki2014]
5. *TBD -- establish acceptance criteria for each gene target based on
   validation results*

### 6.8 Primer and Probe Storage

1. Store primer and probe stocks at --20 C in the designated "Primers"
   cryobox
2. Record all primer information (gene target, primer name, sequence,
   lot number, date received, stock concentration, box/position) in the
   [Freezer Inventory Google Sheet](<!-- LINK_PLACEHOLDER: replace with Google Sheet URL -->)
3. Avoid repeated freeze-thaw of hydrolysis probes; prepare single-use
   aliquots if running assays infrequently
4. Label all tubes with: gene target, primer name (F or R), concentration,
   and date resuspended


## 7. Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

- Every ddPCR run must include: NTC (minimum 2 wells), extraction blank
  (from SOP-L80), and positive control gBlock at a known concentration
- Droplet count per well must exceed 10,000 accepted droplets (out of
  approximately 20,000 generated); wells below this threshold should be
  excluded [@biorad_qx200_2024]
- Positive/negative droplet cluster separation must be unambiguous; set
  the fluorescence amplitude threshold manually using the NTC and
  positive control wells as guides
- *TBD -- define acceptable coefficients of variation for technical
  replicates (typically less than 15% for ddPCR)*
- *TBD -- establish lab-specific LOD and LOQ values for each primer set
  after validation*

## 10. Training Record

Before performing this procedure independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP, [SOP-L80 DNA Extraction](SOP-L80-dna-extraction.qmd),
   and [SOP-L02 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L02-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd)
2. Complete the Bio-Rad QX200 online training modules or equivalent
   manufacturer training
3. Demonstrate competence with the droplet generator, thermal cycler,
   and droplet reader
4. Successfully set up and read a practice plate using positive control
   DNA under supervision
5. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager

## Appendix C: Multiplexing Considerations {.appendix}

When quantifying two gene targets simultaneously (e.g., *amoA* AOB and
*amoA* AOA), use a duplex probe assay with FAM and HEX fluorophores.
Design considerations for multiplexing include:

- Ensure that the two amplicons do not share primer binding sites or
  produce chimeric products
- Optimize annealing temperatures independently before combining; both
  targets must amplify efficiently at the same annealing temperature
- Verify that multiplex results agree with singleplex results within 10%
  using positive control DNA at known concentrations [@dobnik2016]
- *TBD -- document validated multiplex combinations as they are
  developed in the lab*
